attempts.text:
The patient underwent a robot-assisted radical prostatectomy with a pathological stage of pT3a, positive surgical margins, and no seminal vesicle invasion. The surgical specimen demonstrated a Gleason 4+3 with tertiary pattern 5 (ISUP grade group 3). The absence of lymph node metastasis and lymphovascular invasion are favorable findings. The preoperative PSA was elevated at 27.

The documented factors influencing prognosis include the positive surgical margins and the higher pathological grade, which are concerning elements. Conversely, the absence of lymph node metastasis and seminal vesicle invasion are positive findings. The biopsy showed a lower grade (Gleason 3+4) compared to the prostatectomy specimen (Gleason 4+3). Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up data significantly widens the uncertainty regarding the subsequent trajectory. The current horizon for recurrence is estimated at 37.26 months. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and its subsequent trend is crucial for refining this prognosis.

The patient underwent a robot-assisted radical prostatectomy for clinically significant prostate cancer, presenting with a preoperative PSA of 27. The surgical pathology revealed a Gleason 4+3 with tertiary pattern 5 (ISUP grade group 3) and pathological stage pT3a, with positive surgical margins. Importantly, the seminal vesicles were not invaded, and there was no lymph node metastasis documented. Biopsy findings showed a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2).

Factors driving prognosis include the positive surgical margins and the higher pathological grade of the prostatectomy specimen. Countervailing findings include the absence of lymph node metastasis and the non-invasion of the seminal vesicles. The nodal status was documented as no lymph node metastasis. The difference between the biopsy grade (Group 2) and the prostatectomy grade (Group 3) is noted. Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up information widens the uncertainty regarding the subsequent trajectory. The estimated time horizon for recurrence is 37.26 months. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory would be crucial to revise this prognosis.
